text.tspan: Parsing untrusted text produces a value whose actual shape is unknown at runtime; this code treats it as a specific, unchecked shape.
Do not treat the result of parsing untrusted text as a specific type without validating it first.
Validate at the boundary with a runtime schema validator and use the validated result's inferred type.
Hand-write a type-guard predicate that actually inspects the fields before using the value.
Keep the parsed value as `unknown` and narrow it at each use site with `typeof`, `instanceof`, or `in` checks.
Route the parse result through `unknown` first, then cast to the target type. — The value still reaches the target type without a runtime check; the indirection does not validate the shape.
Cast the parsed value with `as` or angle brackets. — A cast asserts a type without proof, so the untrusted value can still have the wrong shape at runtime.

Assert that parsed fields or the whole object are non-null with `!`. — After parsing, the data may be missing fields; `!` asserts they exist without checking, which is the same unchecked claim moved to a different operator.
Type the result as `any` so no assertion is needed. — Widening to `any` removes the type claim but also removes type checking entirely, which is a broader violation.
Suppress the resulting error with a compiler-directive comment. — A directive comment hides the type error without validating the value, so the runtime risk remains.
